title: Logo and Brand Systems in Illustrator
subtitle: For designers building brand identities. Leave with a logo suite and a working brand file.
summary: A one-day workshop that turns a single mark into a working logo system: variants, rules, a delivery pack and a one-page brand sheet.
description_html:
A logo is not a picture. It is a set of files and rules that other people will use without you in the room. This one-day workshop is about building that system in Illustrator: constructing a mark that holds together geometrically, deriving the variants a real brand needs, and delivering it so that a printer, a sign maker and a web developer can each work from the same pack.

The morning is construction. You build a primary mark on a geometric grid, then correct it optically, because a circle drawn to the same measurement as a square looks smaller, and a horizontal stroke matched to a vertical one looks heavier. You then choose and kern a wordmark by eye, outline it, and keep an editable master alongside the outlined version, which is the file most designers forget to keep and later have to rebuild.

The afternoon is where a mark either survives or does not. You produce full-colour, one-colour, reversed and mono variants, define the palette in CMYK, RGB and HEX against a client-supplied Pantone reference, and then run the stress tests: sixteen pixels as a favicon, a single-colour stamp, and signage read from three metres. Anything that fails gets simplified until it works. Clear space and minimum size are drawn as artwork rather than written as a note, because a note gets ignored.

You finish by exporting a delivery pack in AI, EPS, SVG, PDF and PNG under a naming scheme that will still make sense in a year, and by assembling a one-page brand sheet that goes out with it. The day closes with a group critique: you review someone else's mark against the same tests and receive the same in return.

Bring a logo concept or a rough sketch you want to develop. If you have nothing in progress, a written brief and a concept sketch are supplied so that you spend the day building rather than deciding.
outcomes: Construct a primary mark on a geometric grid and correct it optically where the measurements look wrong
Kern a wordmark by eye, outline it, and keep an editable master alongside the outlined artwork
Derive a secondary lockup, a monogram and a horizontal variant from a single primary mark
Produce full-colour, one-colour, reversed and mono versions that stay recognisable in each form
Define a brand palette in CMYK, RGB and HEX against a client-supplied Pantone reference
Test a mark at 16 px, as a single-colour stamp and at three metres, and simplify whichever version fails
Draw clear space and minimum size as artwork rather than describing them in a note
Structure and name the working files so that another designer can open them in a year and understand them
Export a delivery pack in AI, EPS, SVG, PDF and PNG to a consistent naming scheme
Assemble a one-page brand sheet and critique another delegate's mark against the same tests
prerequisites: You should be comfortable in Illustrator already: Pen tool, layers, swatches, type and export. Illustrator Level 2 or equivalent daily experience is the right starting point.
Bring a logo concept or rough sketch you want to develop. A brief and a concept sketch are supplied if you have nothing in progress.
This is a working day rather than a lecture, and it ends with a group critique, so be prepared to show work to the room.
audiences: Designers taking on their first full identity project
In-house designers rebuilding a brand's logo files from whatever was inherited
Freelancers who deliver logos and want a handover pack they can defend
Agency juniors moving from artworking into identity design
Marketing managers who commission logos and keep receiving files they cannot use

faqs.question: Do I need to bring a logo project of my own?
faqs.answer: It is better if you do, because you leave with something you can actually use. Bring a concept, a rough sketch or an existing mark you have been asked to rebuild. If you have nothing in progress, we supply a written brief and a concept sketch so that you spend the day constructing and testing rather than deciding what to draw.

faqs.question: Is one day really enough to design a logo?
faqs.answer: One day is not enough to invent a concept from nothing, and we do not pretend otherwise. It is enough to take a concept that already exists and turn it into a constructed mark, a full set of variants, tested files and a brand sheet. The work we cut is the exploration phase, not the craft.

faqs.question: Do I need a Pantone subscription for the colour session?
faqs.answer: No. Pantone colour books are no longer included with a Creative Cloud subscription and now require a separate Pantone Connect subscription, so we teach the session the way most studios work: you specify CMYK, RGB and HEX yourself and record the Pantone number your client or printer has supplied as a reference. If you do hold Pantone Connect, you can follow along in it.

faqs.question: Is this workshop available self-paced?
faqs.answer: No. The day is built around live construction and a group critique, and neither works as a recorded lesson, so we run it live online, in the Colombo classroom, or privately for a team. You do receive the recording of your own session afterwards for 12 months, along with the templates and checklists.

faqs.question: Do you issue a certificate?
faqs.answer: Yes. You receive a MyLearnPlus certificate of completion naming the workshop, the software version and the hours completed. It is a record of training rather than an Adobe qualification. Adobe Certified Professional certifications are separate exams sat through Certiport.

faqs.question: What if I have to miss the workshop after booking?
faqs.answer: Tell us before the day and we will move you to a later date at no charge. If you miss it without notice you can use your free repeat instead, subject to seats and to the terms shown on the booking page, and the recording is available to you either way.

faqs.question: Can my employer be invoiced, and can you run this for our team?
faqs.answer: Yes. Organisations in Sri Lanka are invoiced in LKR and organisations elsewhere in USD, and we can issue a pro forma invoice against a purchase order. Run privately for a design team, the day can be rebuilt around your own brand: your marks, your press specifications and your existing guidelines.
